title: Wire strict Forest/Fourfold Boolean relations into the existing sparse reference kernel
masterplan_authority: Revision 11 / Version 2.2.0 / Gate 1 — Renovation and owner-directed Genesis
finding: The Fourfold/Tensor contract document explicitly identified a measured adapter from selected Forest/Fourfold relations into the existing TypedRelationBlock kernel as the next useful packet. Until this packet, executable relation-block tests constructed coordinates manually, so the reference kernel was not wired to one exact authoritative Forest/Fourfold subject. Adding another graph schema, relation registry, cache, store, or tensor representation would duplicate authority rather than close this seam.
primary_claim: A narrow Boolean-only adapter now projects one exact Forest/Fourfold subject into the existing TypedRelationBlock oracle without inventing a second relation schema. It requires the exact Forest digest bound by Fourfold, requires complete endpoint planes, uses verified Fourfold bindings for cross-plane relations, uses only directed ForestEdge payloads whose canonical digests are retained by the same-plane Fourfold plane, and refuses retained hyperedges or undirected edges rather than flattening semantics. The adapter grants no trust, approval, promotion, or execution authority.
gardener_decision: Wire the existing Forest, FourfoldSnapshot, RelationSignature, TypedAxis, TypedRelationBlock, and BooleanSemiring surfaces instead of adding another representation. Refuse semantic flattening where the existing contracts cannot preserve completeness, hyperedge shape, direction, or scalar meaning. This replaces ad-hoc manual coordinate construction for an authoritative subject with one bounded seam while deliberately deferring weights, counts, costs, evidence algebra, stores, indices, and backends.
acceptance: a complete exact Fourfold subject projects retained directed same-plane Forest edges into a Boolean TypedRelationBlock matching the direct Forest relation subject
verified cross-plane Fourfold bindings project into a Boolean TypedRelationBlock matching the corresponding direct evidence-backed Forest relation subject
